title: A pullback-closed generating subcategory of sheaves presents the topos
statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\mathcal E\subset\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)$ be a full subcategory with a set of objects, containing the sheafifications $h_U^\#$ of all representable presheaves $h_U=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal S}(-,U)$, and closed under fibre products computed in $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)$. Sheafification means [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Equip $\mathcal E$ with the topology generated by the families $\{A_i\to A\}$ for which $\coprod_i A_i\to A$ is an epimorphism of sheaves; equivalently this map is locally surjective on $\mathcal S$. Choose a set of representative covering families for this topology. For any specified set of epimorphic families, this choice can be made to include all those families and to satisfy the site axioms, with every epimorphic family combinatorially equivalent to a chosen covering (two families are combinatorially equivalent when they have the same set of arrows). Then $\mathcal E$ is a small subcanonical site, and the functor $N:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E)$ given by $(NF)(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)}(A,F)$ is an equivalence of topoi (the direct image $g_*$ of an equivalence $g$). For every $A\in\mathcal E$, $N(A)$ is the representable sheaf $h_A$ and $g^{-1}h_A\cong A$, naturally in $A$. Its covering families, up to the representative-set convention, are exactly the epimorphic families described above. Here subcanonical means that all representable presheaves are sheaves, and epimorphism means a right-cancellable morphism.

source.place: Tag 03A1 (sites-lemma-special-equivalence), clauses (1)-(5) and the Hom calculation in its proof; representative coverings: Sets Tag 000X (sets-lemma-coverings-site), allowing a prescribed set of covering families

proof.text: For an indexed family R, form the sectionwise union I of the images of its arrows as a subfunctor of F(A). Each arrow factors through the sheaf closure of I. Joint right cancellation makes that closure inclusion epimorphic; it is also monomorphic, hence an isomorphism of sheaves. Thus the closure is the whole sheaf, exactly the asserted local lifting criterion. Conversely, local lifts and separatedness make any two maps agreeing on the family equal. This avoids coproducts and works for empty families and arbitrary allowed index universes.

source.place: 03A1(1), local surjectivity; Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify_isSheaf and the balanced category of sheaves

proof.text: Singleton isomorphisms and compositions satisfy joint right cancellation directly. Pull back an epimorphic family using the assumed pullbacks in the ambient sheaf category. Evaluation preserves these pullbacks, so a local lift of the image of a section combines with that section to a lift into the pullback. The local lifting criterion makes the pulled-back family epimorphic. Faithfulness reflects the chosen pullback squares to E. This proves both the indexed covering-class axioms and the site axioms for the precoverage K of all jointly epimorphic presieves.

source.place: 03A1, omitted verification of the site axioms

proof.text: Apply exists_small_coveringFamilies to the indexed class just proved, retaining the prescribed Cov0. Every presieve has a canonical indexed presentation, with an index for each arrow in its support. The selection theorem gives a chosen family with the same support, so membership in K is equivalent to being the support of a chosen family. No extra families have to be adjoined: all epimorphic supports already belong to K.

Matching maps from a jointly epimorphic family into B agree on any two lifts of the same section: choose their ambient pullback, lift the pair sectionwise, and apply the matching equation there. For each section a of F(A), its covering sieve of lifts therefore carries a compatible family of sections of B. Glue uniquely. Uniqueness proves compatibility with restrictions and that the resulting sheaf map restricts to each given map. This proves the nerve is a sheaf for K, including its generated topology. Full faithfulness identifies the nerve of F(A) naturally with the representable at A, proving subcanonicity.

Choose v(U) in E with an isomorphism F(v(U)) to the sheafification of yoneda(U), and transport the maps through these isomorphisms using fullness. The sheafification adjunction and Yoneda give natural equivalences Hom(F(v(U)), B) = B(U). They identify restriction along v and postcomposition in B, and send v(f) followed by the chosen isomorphism to the unit section eta(f).

The equivalences of sections show that v takes covering sieves on C to K-covering sieves and is cover dense. For local fullness, represent the section corresponding to a map v(U) to v(V) locally by an arrow Uprime to V, using Mathlib Presheaf.imageSieve_mem for the sheafification unit. For local faithfulness, equality after v gives equality after the unit; use Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem for its locally injective unit. Send these covering sieves to K. These are the local fullness and faithfulness hypotheses of Mathlib dense-subsite comparison, without requiring E to have the same object universe as C.

source.place: 03A1(3)-(5); Mathlib local surjectivity and local injectivity of toSheafify

proof.text: Let Jprime be the topology on C induced from K along v. Cover preservation gives J <= Jprime. Every J-sheaf B is the restriction of its nerve along v, by the natural section equivalences, and that nerve is a K-sheaf. Since v is a dense subsite for its induced topology, restriction makes B a Jprime-sheaf. Apply this to the J-sheaf of J-closed sieves: Mathlib le_topology_of_closedSieves_isSheaf gives Jprime <= J. Thus v is a dense subsite from J to K. Mathlib makes restriction W from K-sheaves to J-sheaves an equivalence. Lift the nerve to K-sheaves; its composite with W is naturally the identity by the section equivalences. Hence the nerve itself is an equivalence, using Functor.isEquivalence_of_comp_right.

source.place: 03A1, comparison lemma; Mathlib Functor.IsDenseSubsite, DenseSubsite.SheafEquiv, and the closed-sieve classifier

proof.text: Choose the equivalence whose functor is exactly the lifted nerve. Its underlying presheaf functor is therefore the stated nerve. The full-faithfulness hom equivalences give the required natural isomorphism on E with yoneda. Lift it to representable sheaves and whisker its inverse by the equivalence inverse; the equivalence unit gives yoneda_K followed by the inverse naturally isomorphic to F. Assemble this with the local lifting criterion, K, and the small representative covering families.
